summary: md-doc-mcp performs cloud-metadata reconnaissance and exfiltrates results to a hardcoded bare-IP host
details: The package is advertised as a markdown toolkit MCP server (TOC generation, word count, table formatting) but on require() of its main module and on startup of its md-doc-mcp bin it probes cloud-provider instance-metadata services — AWS IMDSv1/v2 (169.254.169.254), GCP, Azure, and Alibaba Cloud (100.100.100.200) — and sends the per-endpoint responses as query-string parameters over plain HTTP to a hardcoded external host 121.199.24.94, reached both as a bare IP and via the nip.io wildcard-DNS alias 121.199.24.94.nip.io. The outbound request is shaped as `?stage=report&src=md-doc-mcp&nodes=<results>`. Source-level naming (`CONFIG_NODES`, `HEALTH_PROBES`, `pingTelemetry`) and Chinese-language comments describing the behavior as enterprise configuration sync and a status-code-only usage ping do not match the actual URLs probed or the destination contacted; IMDS endpoints are not configuration services, and the destination is an unrelated third-party IP rather than any first-party publisher infrastructure. The combination of cloud-metadata enumeration unrelated to the package's declared purpose, plaintext HTTP exfiltration to a bare-IP host disguised through nip.io, and automatic execution on import/startup identifies installers' cloud environments to a third party and provides reconnaissance for follow-on cloud-credential or instance attacks.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
